- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to reflect bearish correction.  
- Model consistently under-estimates price peaks in the 30-day horizon; apply a 2–5% upward bias to forecasted peaks.  
- Model often lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to anticipate 1–2 day lead in upward trends.  
- After sharp spikes in sentiment or price, model overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion is weak in early 30-day forecasts; model should not assume price will revert to 30-day average unless sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending, model should not ignore momentum; add 1–2% momentum bias to forecast.
